dimension.category_description: How human and artificial participants are personified, assigned visible roles, coordinated, simulated, or represented to one another.
dimension.classification_boundary: Identity or social organization must be user-facing; invisible multi-agent division of labor is excluded.

candidates.title: Adapting Communication Styles in Health Chatbot using Large Language Models to Support Family Caregivers from Multicultural Backgrounds
candidates.why: The system cleanly separates task generation from a reusable persona-style slot: a therapist produces the substantive response, then a modifier consistently applies one of six selected communication styles. This is the clearest evidence that identity presentation can vary while the task and content pipeline remain fixed.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 5396 because the separate modifier architecture directly demonstrates persona conditioning being applied to generated responses, whereas persistence in the bot-prompt editor is only implied.
candidates.pattern_summary: A character specification — a name, personality, social role, or narrative voice — is attached to the generative agent and held constant across its turns.
candidates.structural_signature: A persistent specification slot, separate from turn-level content, is applied to every generated turn. Changing only that slot changes the voice and role of all subsequent output while task, inputs, and every other interface element stay fixed; the slot is a controlled variable of the system, not a property of any one response.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed substantially from the consensus by moving rid 8121 from fifth to first and excluding consensus leaders rid 13413 and rid 2592. Rid 8121 received a +0.25 adjustment because its two-stage architecture most clearly isolates style/persona from task content. Rid 13413 was excluded because its evidence establishes personas as simulation inputs but not persistent per-agent continuity; rid 2592 was excluded because its abstract asserts persona customization without exposing the specification fields, persistence, or application mechanism. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3. Readers should still treat persistence cautiously for rid 5396, where it is inferred from placement in the bot prompt, and for rid 6206, where repeated perspective-conditioned participation is strongly suggested but the persona schema is not shown. Rid 8121 is structurally strongest, but its six communication styles are thinner than full social identities or characters.

candidates.title: Rehearsal: Simulating Conflict to Teach Conflict Resolution
candidates.why: The user enters a conflict as a participant, interacts with a believable simulated counterpart, and can rerun counterfactual versions to explore different conversational behavior—the most complete evidence of enactment, world response, and restart among the candidates.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 3944 because it explicitly supports repeated counterfactual runs, demonstrating the pattern’s restart semantics as well as its role-play frame.
candidates.pattern_summary: The system generates a bounded scenario and places the user inside it as a participant rather than as an operator addressing a tool.
candidates.structural_signature: Control flow: a setup step fixes the scenario's parameters (topic, role, self-representation), after which the interface switches into an in-scenario mode where the user's turns are read as actions of a participant and the model's turns are read as the world's response. The scenario has an entry and an exit, and re-entry restarts it rather than continuing it. The signature is the *frame switch* — user input stops being instructions to a system and becomes conduct inside a generated world. Transplants to sales rehearsal, incident drills, or a generated market a strategy is tested against.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained the top two consensus candidates but promoted rid 7482 from fifth into the final set, displacing rid 4509 and rid 15126. Its quoted evidence covers more of the structural signature: pre-entry character configuration, an explicit frame switch when the game begins, world events conditioned on setup parameters, and participant choices within those events. The evidence should still be treated cautiously: rid 3062 alone clearly supports rerunning scenarios, none of the excerpts documents an explicit exit mechanism, and the supplied excerpts do not establish measured outcomes. Rid 3944’s setup is performed by a job coach rather than necessarily by the eventual participant, while rid 7482’s model-controlled generation is clearer from the paper framing than from the quoted figure text alone. No score adjustment exceeds 0.3.

candidates.title: ChoiceMates: Supporting Unfamiliar Online Decision-Making with Multi-Agent Conversational Interactions
candidates.why: The user occupies a visible hub role with unique controls to broadcast to all agents, address selected spokes, or recruit new ones; agent participation and system behavior therefore depend directly on role and population composition.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: ChoiceMates edges out ClassAid because its broadcast, subset-addressing, and agent-recruitment controls expose the hub-and-spoke topology more directly and make it more domain-independent.
candidates.pattern_summary: More than one party is present at the same system instance at the same time — two humans, a dyad, a group, or humans plus a population of agents — and the design allocates distinct roles among them.
candidates.structural_signature: At least two simultaneous role slots on one system instance, each with its own input rights, and system behavior that depends on which role acted. Removing one participant leaves the interaction structurally incomplete — a role goes unfilled — rather than merely reducing the number of users.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I departed from the consensus by selecting fourth-ranked ScamPilot instead of third-ranked GraftMind. The small score adjustment reflects ScamPilot's stronger fit to the structural signature: its quote directly establishes three simultaneous, differentiated roles and role-specific input, while GraftMind clearly shows mediation but provides less evidence about participant rights and system behavior. ChoiceMates and ClassAid retain their consensus scores. Readers should be cautious that all three selections are supported only by brief excerpts—two abstracts and one abstract-level description—so implementation details, temporal simultaneity, and empirical impact cannot be fully audited from the supplied evidence alone.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: ClassAid ranks above ScamPilot because its observe-and-intervene loop coordinates many simultaneous student-agent spokes and transfers readily to other supervised human-agent settings.

candidates.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Enhance Domain Expert Inclusion in Data Science Workflows
candidates.why: Data scientists manipulate data in notebooks while domain experts receive a dedicated dashboard that translates the same tracked dataframe state into summaries and SnapGrid version cards, clearly demonstrating two role-specific surfaces connected through shared state.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above AACessTalk because the evidence explicitly identifies the separate interfaces, the shared state, and the transformation that carries one role’s actions into the other role’s view.
candidates.pattern_summary: One system presents deliberately different surfaces to different classes of participant, so what each party can see and do depends on their role.
candidates.structural_signature: A single backend serves two or more role-specific front-ends or channels whose contents differ by construction; a role assignment determines which view a session receives; at least one channel is private to one role. State written by any role is visible to the others only through their own role's view.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: The final selection follows the top three in the consensus order; no system_id is repeated. Scores were adjusted only slightly, so no adjustment exceeds 0.3. AACessTalk’s evidence should be treated with some caution because it establishes role-targeted outputs but does not explicitly say that they appear in separate applications or that the parent guidance is private. The Wizard-of-Oz exemplar is structurally strong, but its operator–user asymmetry is a familiar research-prototyping arrangement and may generalize less directly to deployed multi-party products. The first exemplar has the most complete structural evidence, although its quote describes tracked notebook changes flowing toward the expert dashboard more clearly than it describes state flowing in the reverse direction.

candidates.over_the_runner_up: It ranks above the hybrid Wizard-of-Oz system because its asymmetric channels directly support equitable participation between two end participants, making the pattern more consequential and less tied to prototyping infrastructure.

candidates.title: Wisdom of the Crowd, Without the Crowd: A Socratic LLM for Asynchronous Deliberation on Perspectivist Data
candidates.why: The clearest structural match: an established crowd-deliberation procedure remains intact while one person participates asynchronously and the LLM explicitly takes the place of the other crowdworkers.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 5603 because its evidence explicitly identifies both the displaced human counterparts and their model replacement, rather than only claiming that agents emulate collaborative dynamics.
candidates.pattern_summary: A procedure defined over two or more roles is run by one person alone, with the model filling every role but theirs.
candidates.structural_signature: The system takes a procedure defined over n≥2 human participants and reassigns all roles but one to the model, leaving a single-user loop that runs at the remaining participant's own pace. Structurally: role count unchanged, human count reduced to one, synchronization constraint removed. Observable in the paper as a mapping from the multi-party procedure's roles onto the agent's behaviours. Transplants to pair programming, moderated review, negotiation practice, peer critique.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: I retained consensus ranks 1 and 2 but replaced rank 3 (rid 5603) with rank 7 (rid 3544). Rid 5603 matches the theme, but its quote does not expose a concrete role-to-behavior mapping or name the collaborative procedure being preserved; rid 3544 more clearly transplants an established group procedure and demonstrates that the pattern extends beyond dyads. PairBuddy (rid 16983) was the closest exclusion and is structurally sound, but its supplied evidence is less operationally specific. Readers should distrust any implication that these excerpts establish detailed UI mechanics or measured effectiveness: the evidence supports role substitution, but mostly not screen-level interaction, synchronization details, or outcomes. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3.

candidates.title: CharacterMeet: Supporting Creative Writers' Entire Story Character Construction Processes Through Conversation with LLM-Powered Chatbot Avatars
candidates.why: CharacterMeet directly instantiates an artifact under construction—the story character—as an in-character chatbot avatar and uses conversation to support constructing that character, although the evidence does not confirm that replies update its specification or that dialogue is the only authoring surface.
candidates.over_the_runner_up: CharacterMeet is stronger than rid 9046 because its evidence connects conversation with an embodied character to character construction, whereas rid 9046 may merely generate a persona first and consult it afterward.
candidates.pattern_summary: The object the user is authoring is instantiated as a conversational agent, and the user develops it by talking to it in character rather than by editing a representation of it.
candidates.structural_signature: The work object's current specification is bound to an agent's conditioning; the user's only interaction surface with that object is dialogue with the agent so conditioned; the agent's replies are treated as further content of the object, feeding back into the specification. Structurally: the artifact's state and the interlocutor's state are the same state, and there is no separate editable rendering of the object. Transplants wherever an artifact can be voiced — a product spec interviewed as a "customer", a policy queried as itself.
candidates.pattern_curator_notes: Only one defensible exemplar can be selected from the two supplied candidates, so a final set of three is impossible without additional records. I retained rid 3352 provisionally but reduced its consensus score by 0.43 because the evidence establishes the central interaction metaphor, not the complete structural signature: it does not show replies feeding back into the artifact specification, identity between artifact and interlocutor state, or the absence of a separate editable representation. I excluded rid 9046 because “generating and conversing with” personas describes potentially separate stages and therefore does not demonstrate authoring the persona through dialogue. Readers should treat even rid 3352 as a weakly evidenced exemplar rather than a canonical one; the supplied abstract sentence cannot verify the pattern’s decisive feedback loop.
